result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Use message events for directed participant communication, signal events for broadcasts, and timer events for stated dates, durations or cycles.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

result.rule: When the description states that a process can end in one of multiple mutually exclusive outcomes: Model an exclusive gateway with a separate branch for each outcome, leading to the corresponding modeled outcome.

When the description states that an activity's result or a condition determines which of multiple alternative paths follows: Connect the activity to an exclusive gateway and model each alternative as a separate outgoing branch.
When the description states that an action has mutually exclusive alternatives for how or where it is carried out: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway and a separate task for each alternative.

When the description states that a process can begin through alternative channels before continuing through a shared flow: Model each channel as a separate branch and merge the branches with an exclusive gateway before the shared flow.
